newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU opens probe into GAN's new rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: EU opens probe into GAN's new rescue plan.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had started a probe into France's proposed plan to grant up to 20 billion francs ($3.5 billion) to state-controlled insurer GAN to prepare it for privatisation.

In September last year the Commission had already approved a 2.8-billion-franc state recapitalisation of GAN in 1995 on the assumption that the firm would divest its majority stake in bank Credit Industriel et Commercial (CIC) before being sold itself.

But the French state jumped to the rescue of the troubled insurer again last month announcing it would make a capital injection of 11 billion francs to avoid a deterioration of its financial situation. Another nine billion would cover estimated losses.
"Such measures appear necessary for the survival of GAN given that the 1996 restructuring plan seems to have failed," the Commission said in a statement.

GAN, whose problems stem mainly from its UIC property financing unit, is expecting to post a net attributable loss of five billion francs for 1996. The group suffered a loss of 1.8 billion francs in 1995 and 5.3 billion the previous year.
The Commission said that without the new aid, GAN's losses in 1996 would have amounted to 15 billion francs.

The Commission must vet all national government plans to rescue ailing, often state-owned, companies. It is usually inclined to approve such plans if they are limited to restoring the long-term viability of the aided companies and if privatisation is in sight.
French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said in February that the government planned to privatise GAN along with CIC "during the course of 1997".
The Commission gave the French government a month to provide it with a "realistic and detailed restructuring plan". ($1 = 5.74 FRF)
